_comment: Hand-curated corrections to what the survey mine produces. Small on purpose:
everything here is a case where the source markup is genuinely ambiguous and
no rule reads it correctly, so the decision is recorded rather than inferred.

FRAGMENTS. A loot cell like 'Mithril Vambraces
Greaves' means two items

sharing a prefix, and 'Torn Page of Mastery
Earth · Water · Fire · Wind'
means one item with four variants. Splitting on the separator produced items
called Earth, Fire, Water, Wind, Skin, Sleeves, Greaves and 'pg. 3' - each
with its own page, canonical URL and share card.
We do NOT reconstruct the full names. 'Mithril Greaves' is a guess and
'Torn Page of Mastery: Earth' invents a naming format. Instead the fragment
is attached to the row it came from, suppressed from the A-Z, and printed on
the parent's page as what the source actually says.
FRAGMENT_RESOLVED is that rule being retired one entry at a time, on
evidence. An /outputfile inventory dump is the game's own record of an item
name, so where a dump holds the full name, the fragment stops being a
fragment and becomes an ordinary item with its own page. Four are resolved
and the guess would have been wrong twice: the format is 'Torn Page of
Mastery Fire' with no colon, and 'Sleeves' beside an Embroidered Black Cape
is an Embroidered Black SLEEVES, a different garment, not the cape.
Earth and Wind stay unresolved deliberately. We now know the naming format
from two confirmed siblings, and applying it to the other two would be a
pattern inference rather than a reading. They are one dump away.
GROUPS are row headings, not items: a cell reading 'Bronze weapon line' names
a family whose members are listed beside it.
ALIASES merge one entity that the source spells two ways. The bar is that
the two spellings describe the SAME record, not two records that share a
story. Zordak Ragefire was aliased to Zordakalicus Ragefire here and that
was wrong: the survey gives them different levels (60 and 54), different
locations, different races (HUMAN MERCHANT and LAVA DRAGON) and different
behaviour (a non-aggressive vendor and a triggered spawn). They are one
character in the Cleric epic and two entries in the game, and merging them
pointed both rows at one page, so whichever built last erased the other.
Withdrawn 11 Aug 2026. A shared surname is not a spelling variant.
To add a case: put the exact mined name on the left. scripts/check.py fails
if a name here no longer appears in the data, so this file cannot rot quietly.
